items.title: 68002_Benny Waters oral history interview
items.q: Would you say the solos of Driver, Lee and yourself in the Charlie Miller Jazz Orchestra

ctx.x: That somebody could be in a school. Would you say the solos of Driver, Lee and yourself in the Charlie Miller Jazz Orchestra, we're speaking of the 'teens now, late 'teens in Philadelphia, were of the same school or more primitive in nature in what a jazz solo was to the innovations of Bechet and Armstrong that we hear on records a few years later?

Well, I would say it was a little bit different, see. But Bill, Bill Lee could play a much, very much trumpet, a lot of trumpet, and he improvised real well in correct harmonies. But it didn't sound like Louis Armstrong. And I could play a lot of saxophone and improvise, but I wasn't copying Sidney Bechet because I didn't hear much of, that much of those, that period, you see what i mean? So that's what I'm saying, that [ ] -
